Thanks for the context. Reviewing the forecast quickly, a few product/platform asks before we lock in the multiplier:

1) Peak profile: Emily, can you provide the top-3 hourly windows you expect traffic to concentrate in (UTC preferred)? We tune kernel selection and batch sizes around those windows.
2) Model variant strategy: Do you plan to use a single model throughout or degrade to a smaller quantized variant under pressure? If you can tolerate a variant fallback, we can keep latency SLOs tighter while preserving throughput.
3) Cacheable prefixes: Any predictable prefixes (e.g., user onboarding prompts) we should add to prefix cache? If so, provide a list of up to 50 common prefixes to pre-warm.
4) SLA carveout scope: we typically support a temporary uplift under a soft-SLA (reduced uptime guarantees) if a mutual action plan is signed and we get an emergency contact. Standard carveout items: time window, multiplier, max sustained tokens/min, and rollback criteria.

Operationally, product needs:
- A measurement day (sample hour with live traffic) one week prior to launch to validate assumptions.
- A single escalation contact at Ember (SRE lead) and an internal Redwood runbook owner.

If those items look OK, we can provision the uplift and document the exact throttle bands. Marissa — can you draft the mutual action plan and share a one-pager for Emily to sign?

Irene Choi
Head of Product, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
